facts.claim: Department of Agriculture, Biosecurity Advice 2018-12 (11 July 2018): 'Import conditions require importers to manage biosecurity risk before they send cut flowers and foliage to Australia, thereby reducing the number of pests that arrive at our borders.' The same page: 'With this trade comes the potential to introduce unwanted pests and diseases into Australia.'

Department of Agriculture, Biosecurity Advice 2018-12: 'An analysis of inspection records showed that a high proportion of imported fresh cut flowers and foliage have been infested with quarantine pests (including thrips, aphids and mites)'. 'The amended import conditions are available on the Biosecurity Import Conditions system (BICON).'

Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry, List of species of fresh cut flowers and foliage with alternative conditions for import (mainland): the list 'contains conditionally non-prohibited goods which as subject to specific conditions of import' and 'Importers should consult BICON for the full range of import conditions for all goods intended for import.'

AgriFutures Australia, project 'Farm-based methods for control of flowering in Waratahs' (The University of Sydney, closed): waratah flowering is concentrated in spring; expected outcomes include 'reduction of oversupply in Spring and ability to capitalise on early and late season prices'. The project aimed to extend flowering 'to meet peak demand periods, such as Christmas and Valentine's Day'.

Bureau of Meteorology, Solstices, equinoxes and the seasons (updated 17 September 2026, read 20 November 2026): 'Australian summer, autumn, winter and spring are defined as: summer – the warmest 3 months: December, January and February; winter – the coolest 3 months: June, July and August; spring and autumn – the 3-month transition periods between summer and winter.'
Bureau of Meteorology, same page: 'for Australia it's a better fit with our temperatures to use 1 March, 1 June, 1 September and 1 December' to start each season.

Bureau of Meteorology, same page: 'For Australia's northern tropics ... the European 4-season model isn't relevant.' The year is divided into a 'wet season' (October to April) and a 'dry season' (May to September).

insider_details.detail: Imported stems travel through a biosecurity system: the department's own records found a high proportion of imported cut flowers carried quarantine pests such as thrips, aphids and mites, and importers must manage that risk before shipping. Ask your florist early how imported varieties are sourced so a held or failed consignment doesn't leave a gap in your arrangements.
Waratahs are a spring flower in Australia, and growers have long tried to stretch the season because supply peaks then. A spring wedding is the natural time to feature them locally grown.
